verdict.rationale: Okta's Event Hooks provide outbound webhook calls triggered by specified org events, enabling automated actions to be wired up when events occur, and the MCP server/agent examples show event-driven queries (e.g., failed logins) being actioned via AI agents. However, this is infrastructure for building rule-triggered automations rather than a native, user-facing 'if this event then this action' rules engine tailored for AI-native users. Missing for 10: a documented no-code/low-code rule builder for event-to-action automation, first-party examples of AI agents autonomously defining and executing such rules, and independent/hands-on confirmation of this workflow.
